title: What is MCR-L?
text: MCR-L means Mathematical Cognitive Resonance for Language. It is an experimental CPU-first symbolic and structured language-reasoning prototype inspired by the recurrent situation model in SCENT-X MCR-2. It parses a bounded set of intents, activates explicit semantic signals, retrieves indexed evidence, scores structured answer plans, and realizes answers with controlled grammar templates. It does not load a neural language model.
answer: MCR-L (Mathematical Cognitive Resonance for Language) is an experimental CPU-first language-reasoning system. It separates semantic parsing, recurrent situation modelling, indexed evidence retrieval, answer-plan scoring, verification, and controlled language realization. Its first prototype uses explicit rules rather than a pretrained neural language model.

title: Does MCR-L require a GPU?
text: The MCR-L 0.1 prototype uses Python standard-library code, explicit rules, recurrent scalar activations, and SQLite retrieval. It does not load a neural language model or require a dedicated GPU for inference. CPU time and RAM are still required. Speed and answer coverage depend on database size, indexing, question complexity, and the rule system.
answer: MCR-L 0.1 does not require a dedicated GPU. Its inference path uses CPU-executable rules, small recurrent state calculations, and SQLite retrieval. It still needs a CPU, memory, and storage, and this does not prove that every future version or every AI workload can run efficiently on a laptop.

title: What is the difference between a CPU and GPU?
text: A CPU is a general-purpose processor designed for varied sequential and parallel tasks. A GPU contains many processing units designed to perform large numbers of similar operations in parallel. A GPU can accelerate neural-network matrix operations, graphics, and other parallel workloads, but a GPU is not required for every AI system.
answer: A CPU is a general-purpose processor suited to varied tasks and control flow. A GPU is designed to execute many similar operations in parallel, which makes it useful for graphics and large neural-network computations. A rule-based or retrieval-based AI can run on a CPU without a dedicated GPU, although speed depends on the workload.

title: How should a 2–3 GB language database be stored?
text: A multi-gigabyte language and knowledge corpus should be ingested incrementally, cleaned, deduplicated, segmented, and indexed. Keep source, author, date, licence, domain, and confidence metadata. Use an on-disk database such as SQLite with FTS5, memory-mapped indexes, or another inverted index. Do not load the entire corpus into RAM for every question. Plain text volume alone does not guarantee factual accuracy or semantic coverage.
answer: Do not load a 2–3 GB language corpus into RAM for every question. Stream it into an on-disk indexed store, split content into useful records, remove duplicates, and preserve source, date, domain, and licence metadata. Retrieve only the relevant records at inference time. The corpus must be curated: more text does not automatically mean better reasoning or more reliable facts.

title: Why can a computer slow down when a game opens?
text: A computer may slow down when a game opens because the game increases CPU, GPU, memory, disk, or thermal load. Possible causes include a CPU bottleneck, GPU saturation, insufficient RAM leading to paging, background tasks, storage delays, driver problems, or thermal throttling. The actual cause cannot be identified without measurements such as CPU/GPU utilization, memory use, temperatures, clocks, and frame times.
answer: A game can make a computer slow down by increasing CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, and cooling demands. Common possibilities include a CPU or GPU bottleneck, memory pressure, background processes, slow asset loading, driver issues, or thermal throttling. These are possibilities, not a diagnosis. Check CPU and GPU utilization, RAM use, temperatures, clock speeds, and frame-time data while the slowdown occurs.

title: What is a recurrent situation model?
text: A recurrent situation model maintains a bounded internal activation vector across successive observations. A new state depends on the current input features, the previous activations, and weighted relationships between signals. This can encode persistence and interaction, but it does not automatically create understanding: useful behavior depends on feature quality, weight design, objectives, and validation.
answer: A recurrent situation model keeps a numerical state across observations. Each update combines new input features with previous activations and weighted relationships between signals. This gives the system a form of state and context persistence, but it does not automatically produce understanding; the features, relationships, objectives, and evaluation tests must be designed well.

title: Does a large dictionary or text corpus make an AI intelligent?
text: A dictionary or large text collection provides lexical entries and examples, but it does not by itself supply reliable world knowledge, causal models, grounding, planning, or the ability to generalize. A system needs structured representations, retrieval, inference procedures, provenance, uncertainty handling, and empirical evaluation. Corpus size alone is not a measure of intelligence.
answer: No. A large dictionary or text collection supplies words, definitions, and examples, but it does not automatically provide reliable world knowledge, causal reasoning, grounding, planning, or generalization. Those capabilities require explicit representations and inference mechanisms, evidence tracking, uncertainty handling, and testing. Corpus size alone is not a measure of intelligence.

title: What are the limitations of MCR-L 0.1?
text: MCR-L 0.1 is a rule-based and retrieval-based research baseline. Its semantic parser recognizes a limited set of English cues, its knowledge coverage depends on imported records, and its answer planner can only select evidence that retrieval finds. It does not understand arbitrary paraphrases, learn language from raw books, reason reliably over all domains, or replace a trained general-purpose language model.
answer: MCR-L 0.1 is a limited research prototype, not a general-purpose conversational AI. It recognizes a small set of English patterns, retrieves from its supplied knowledge records, and builds answers from those records. It cannot reliably understand arbitrary paraphrases, learn language directly from raw books, or answer questions outside its indexed knowledge. Those are explicit targets for future research, not current capabilities.
